title: Summer Camp Story Circle Kit - Middle Activity Lane

activities.title: Acorn Errand Relay Circle
activities.circleSkill: Sequencing a shared quest with clear handoff details
activities.sessionFit: 18-minute opening circle for a cabin table, rec program group, or co-op writing block.
activities.counselorSetup: Print one page per writer, choose a talking object, and mark three imaginary errand stops on the circle board.
activities.kidDirection: Add one errand clue, pass the story to the next writer, and help the acorn office finish its route.
activities.counselorPrompt: Ask each writer to give the next person one useful detail instead of solving the whole route.

pageSections.heading: Errand Start
lines: The first tiny errand asks for ____________________________.

pageSections.heading: Circle Handoff
lines: I pass the next clue by adding ____________________________.
The next helper should check near ____________________________.
One detail everyone should remember is ____________________________.

pageSections.heading: Route Finish
lines: The acorn clerk thanks the group for ____________________________.

activities.groupTwistLine: When the talking object reaches the counselor, add a surprise errand from ____________________________.
activities.wrapUpLine: The handoff detail that helped the circle most was ____________________________.
activities.quietOptionLine: Instead of passing aloud, write the next route clue on ____________________________.

activities.title: Button Bakery Map Mixup Circle
activities.circleSkill: Using map language and specific nouns in a group story
activities.sessionFit: 20-minute after-lunch circle when the group needs a low-prep shared writing activity.
activities.counselorSetup: Sketch a simple bakery counter, crumb path, and button tray before handing out pages.
activities.kidDirection: Choose one bakery clue, add a direction word, and help the group fix the mixed-up map.
activities.counselorPrompt: Invite writers to replace vague clues with objects the whole circle can picture.

pageSections.heading: Bakery Map
lines: The map points past a tray of ____________________________.

pageSections.heading: Direction Clues
lines: Turn left when the group sees ____________________________.

pageSections.heading: Map Fix
lines: The best clue from the circle is ____________________________.
The bakery route finally leads to ____________________________.

activities.groupTwistLine: Halfway through, trade maps with a neighbor and add one clear landmark: ____________________________.
activities.wrapUpLine: The strongest map word I used today was ____________________________.
activities.quietOptionLine: Work silently by drawing arrows first, then write the route clue ____________________________.

activities.title: Seed Library Packet Circle
activities.circleSkill: Combining setting clues, cause, and next action
activities.sessionFit: 22-minute shaded-table activity for older elementary writers who can build on each other's ideas.
activities.counselorSetup: Set out pencils and invite the group to imagine a seed library with drawers, ladders, and map pins.
activities.kidDirection: Invent one seed packet, explain why it matters, and pass the next map-room action to the circle.
activities.counselorPrompt: Ask writers to connect each new seed clue to a next step the map keeper can take.

pageSections.heading: Packet Clue
lines: Inside the packet, the group finds ____________________________.

pageSections.heading: Why It Matters
lines: The next drawer opens only after ____________________________.

pageSections.heading: Circle Action
lines: The map changes when someone adds ____________________________.
The seed library story moves toward ____________________________.

activities.groupTwistLine: Let one writer become the map keeper and choose the next drawer: ____________________________.
activities.wrapUpLine: One cause-and-next-step link from my page is ____________________________.
activities.quietOptionLine: For a quiet round, point to a map spot and write the seed clue ____________________________.

activities.title: Greenhouse Gear Garden Build
activities.circleSkill: Adding problem-solving steps without turning the story into a contest
activities.sessionFit: 20-minute maker-style story circle for camp tables, art rooms, or garden-theme afternoons.
activities.counselorSetup: Draw three harmless garden gadgets on a board and remind writers that silly fixes are welcome.
activities.kidDirection: Choose a garden gadget, describe what it does, and add one cooperative repair step.
activities.counselorPrompt: Ask how the gadget helps the group and what gentle problem it creates next.

pageSections.heading: Garden Gadget
lines: The greenhouse gear is shaped like ____________________________.
The first sound it makes is ____________________________.

pageSections.heading: Gentle Problem
lines: The group notices the small problem when ____________________________.
A helpful tool on the table is ____________________________.

pageSections.heading: Repair Step
lines: Next, the gear garden helper tries ____________________________.

activities.groupTwistLine: Add a second gadget that only works when two writers agree on ____________________________.
activities.wrapUpLine: The cooperative repair step I liked best was ____________________________.
activities.quietOptionLine: Sketch the gadget quietly, then label the repair idea ____________________________.

activities.title: Index Card Theater Scene Circle
activities.circleSkill: Building a tiny scene with dialogue, stage action, and turn-taking
activities.sessionFit: 25-minute indoor camp option for hot afternoons, rain delays, or theater-themed rotations.
activities.counselorSetup: Give each writer a pretend index card role and set a rule that every scene stays kind and playful.
activities.kidDirection: Pick a role card, write one line of dialogue, and pass the scene so the next writer can move it forward.
activities.counselorPrompt: Ask writers to make each line change what the characters do next.

pageSections.heading: Role Card
lines: My theater card gives me the role of ____________________________.

pageSections.heading: Dialogue Turn
lines: The line changes the scene by ____________________________.

pageSections.heading: Stage Action
lines: At the start, the character moves toward ____________________________.
In the middle, the group reacts to ____________________________.

activities.groupTwistLine: After two turns, the counselor adds a new prop card: ____________________________.
activities.wrapUpLine: The dialogue line that moved the scene forward was ____________________________.
activities.quietOptionLine: Act nothing out; write the stage action quietly as ____________________________.

activities.title: Penny Path Compass Circle
activities.circleSkill: Choosing direction words and sensory details for a shared route
activities.sessionFit: 18-minute trailhead or picnic-table writing circle before a walk, game, or craft.
activities.counselorSetup: Place a pretend compass in the center and assign north, south, east, and west spots around the circle.
activities.kidDirection: Spin the compass, choose a path clue, and add one detail that helps the group follow the route.
activities.counselorPrompt: Ask each writer to include one direction word and one detail a reader could hear, see, or feel.

pageSections.heading: Compass Spin
lines: The first path marker looks like ____________________________.

pageSections.heading: Route Detail
lines: A sound along the path is ____________________________.

activities.groupTwistLine: Let the next writer reverse one direction and explain the new clue: ____________________________.
activities.wrapUpLine: The direction detail that made my route clearer was ____________________________.
activities.quietOptionLine: Trace the compass path silently, then write one route sentence: ____________________________.
